steps.prompt: What is the smallest value $x^2$ can take? What about $(x - 3)^2 + 5$? For which $x$ does it happen?
steps.placeholder: The smallest value… it happens when…

cards.title: Make a perfect square
cards.body: $(x + h)^2 = x^2 + 2hx + h^2$. So take HALF the $x$ coefficient, square it, and add and take it away: $x^2 + 6x + 2 = (x^2 + 6x + 9) - 9 + 2 = (x + 3)^2 - 7$.

cards.title: The vertex is the lowest (or highest) point
cards.body: A square is never negative, so $a(x - h)^2 + k$ with $a > 0$ is smallest when $x = h$, and its smallest value is $k$. With $a < 0$ the parabola opens down and $k$ is the LARGEST value. Shortcut: the vertex is at $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$; put that $x$ back in to get the value.

cards.title: Worked example: the smallest value
cards.problem: What is the smallest value of $2x^2 - 12x + 5$?

cards.title: The common trap: where vs how much
cards.body: The smallest VALUE is $k$; the $x$ where it happens is $h$. Read which one the question wants. $(x - 5)^2$ means $h = +5$. And when $a \neq 1$, take $a$ out of the $x$ terms first: $2x^2 - 12x = 2(x^2 - 6x)$.

prompts: Explain to a friend why $(x - h)^2 + k$ can never be smaller than $k$.
